rooms.long: The defiled remains of a final refuge.
A low arch of stone stands ahead, its carved face worn smooth by rain. Broken cobbles and weeded ruts mark the road leading toward the silent city.
The vaulting of the gatehouse is blackened with soot and age, and the portcullis is long gone. Light spills through gaps above where beams have fallen.
The old thoroughfare begins in cracked stone and scattered gravel. A line of shutterless facades leans inward, their plaster peeled away.
A narrow street of pale stone stretches between blank walls. Rusted iron brackets jut where balconies once hung.
Two streets meet in a small square of cracked paving. An empty fountain base sits crooked against the curb.
The road widens here, its center sunk and filled with damp leaves. A fallen signboard lies half-buried in the grit.
Low buildings crowd the street, their doorways gaping and dark. Rainwater gathers in the ruts where carts once passed.
A second gate rises ahead, its guardwalk broken and open to the sky. Weed-choked steps lead through the arch.
Paving stones are missing in patches, leaving uneven earth. A stretch of wrought iron railing clings to one wall, bent inward.
A side lane cuts west toward narrower houses. The corner stones are chipped and slick with lichen.
The lane pinches between tall, close walls of mottled stone. A ribbon of ivy trails down from a broken cornice.
The street stays in shadow beneath overhanging roofs. Damp plaster flakes from the walls in thin curls.
The lane narrows to a bend where the stones are nearly buried. A collapsed stoop leaves a shallow pit of rubble.
Unfinished walls stand in a rough square, their mortar crumbled into dust. Timber scaffolds lie splintered across the ground.
A stout stone building squats behind a collapsed lintel. Rusted hooks and empty racks line the interior walls.
The street opens to a small intersection marked by worn corner stones. Broken shutters hang from a nearby window frame.
A broad band of stone runs between mute facades. Drifts of grit and leaves gather along the curb.
The paving here is pale and smoothed by time. A cracked column base lies beside a doorway.
Dust lies thick in the seams between stones. A sagging awning frame still clings to a wall.
Old iron rails bracket the street, many bent or missing. The road is scarred by shallow ruts.
The street widens into a square of mottled stone. A dry basin sits at the center, its rim chipped and stained.
Shuttered storefronts line the way, their thresholds choked with weeds. The stone is slick where rainwater pools.
Faded plaster clings to the walls in torn patches. A thin vine threads across a cracked arch.
Two streets intersect around a scatter of broken paving. A split wagon wheel rests in the gutter.
The street tightens, squeezed by leaning masonry. Loose slate tiles litter the edges of the road.
The intersection is marked by a low stone post worn smooth. Thin grass pushes up through the central joints.
A straight lane runs east and west through close-set houses. The walls show traces of pale paint and old murals.
The lane is littered with fragments of tile and brick. A broken archway opens into a hollowed shop.
The street ends at a tumbled wall where stones have slid down. A narrow alley slips away beside the ruin.
The road here is uneven, with stones heaved by roots. A bent streetlamp rises from a base of cracked stone.
A high arch leads toward the inner rise of the city. The guard slots are empty, their stone edges crumbled.
The road climbs slightly, flanked by taller facades. Broken balcony ironwork hangs over the street.
Two roads meet before a line of long, low buildings. Their doorways gape, dark and silent.
Long stone halls march along the street, their roofs partly fallen. Rusted nails and timbers lie in heaps.
The street is broader here, with a strip of packed earth between stones. A toppled post leans against a wall.
The road runs straight between crumbling barracks. Wind has pushed leaves into slow drifts.
The row of barracks breaks down into broken foundations. A sagging gate frame stands without doors.
A pit of rubble and half-set stone marks an abandoned build. Weeds knot around a snapped beam.
The road narrows as the surrounding walls thin. A fragment of mosaic tile glints among the dust.
The town gate's stone throat opens above, its portcullis long vanished. Rain has carved dark trails down the blocks.
Broken paving leads up to the archway, scattered with fallen masonry. The flanking towers stand cracked and hollow.
The street is lined with long foundations and collapsed roofs. Rusted iron hoops lie in the dirt.
The buildings here are little more than low walls. Grass grows thick where floors once lay.
A wide track of stone holds pooled rainwater. A shattered doorway arches into darkness.
The stone is cracked and uneven, with weeds in the seams. A line of iron pegs runs along one wall.
The road ends near a heap of collapsed roof tiles. A rusted bell frame tilts in the rubble.
The lane is straight and silent, edged by worn thresholds. A chipped well cap sits off to one side.
A tight passage squeezes between two leaning walls. The stone here is smooth with wear and damp.
A small lane winds between cramped houses. Broken shutters lie in the weeds.
The lane is edged by low brickwork and crumbling steps. A faded tile pattern lingers in the dust.
The lane opens toward a wider street, its stones chipped and uneven. A sagging lintel hangs over a dark doorway.
A small hall opens here with a low stage and a cracked rail. Tattered curtains hang in strips along the back wall.
The street bends past a row of battered lamp posts and narrow doors. Faded plaster still carries traces of painted vines.
A wide room holds a chipped dance floor and a sagging balcony. Dust coats the rail where hands once rested.
A small guard nook overlooks the outer road, its slit windows broken and widened by time. Dusty stone benches remain where sentries once rested.
A tight stairwell spirals upward through the west tower, its steps worn into shallow cups. The air carries the scent of damp stone and old ash.
The landing opens onto two dark passages with flaked plaster. A fallen torch bracket lies on the floor.
This passage runs along the upper wall, with gaps where the parapet has crumbled. Wind slips through the open stonework.
A steep stair climbs the western spire, the inner wall scarred by old tool marks. Loose rubble gathers in the corners.
The roof is bare to the sky, ringed by a broken parapet. Pooled rainwater glints in shallow basins.
Broad steps descend through the gatehouse, cracked and uneven. A strip of faded tile clings to the wall.
A long chamber lies open and empty, its ceiling partially collapsed. Soot stains the stone where braziers once burned.
Wide windows face the street, their frames hanging loose and bare. Bits of colored plaster remain on the walls, muted by age.
Long tables are gone, but their scars remain in the floor. A hearth stands cold beneath a chipped mantle.
Low bunks have collapsed into heaps of wood and straw. The air carries a trace of old straw and dust.
A narrow passage runs along the inner wall, lit by a broken slit. Fine grit lies under fallen plaster.
A broad walk runs along the inner wall, its stone railing cracked and low. Ornate ironwork curves still cling to a few posts.
Stone steps climb within the eastern tower, their edges worn thin. A trickle of water runs down one wall.
The base of the eastern stairwell is ringed with fallen tiles. The doorway to the yard stands doorless and warped.
A wide street runs between elegant facades, their arches chipped and open. Wrought iron balconies sag above the broken paving.
The stairwell narrows as it rises, with crumbling plaster exposing rough stone. Iron nails protrude where a railing once stood.
The roof of the eastern spire is open to the weather, its parapet broken. A lone flagpole lies across the stones.
A small chamber holds a cracked basin and a warped doorway. The walls are stained by long-dry smoke.
A guard niche watches the road through a broken arrow slit. The ledge is slick with damp and moss.
A side chamber sits empty except for scattered rubble. The plaster has peeled away in long, curling strips.
Hooks and empty racks line the walls of this small armoury. The floor is strewn with rust flakes and rot.
The broad street narrows toward the western gate, its paving cracked. Shuttered archways watch over the quiet way.
A stone stair rises along a battered wall, its steps chipped and damp. A broken lantern hook hangs above the landing.
This cramped room has a narrow slit for light and a floor of cracked stone. Water stains run down the corners.
A small chamber opens off the stair, bare and silent. A broken latch hangs from the doorframe.
The chamber is broad but empty, with a roof caved in at one end. Charred beams lie across the floor.
The landing connects two stairwells, its stone worn smooth. A length of collapsed railing rests against the wall.
The stairwell winds downward in the west wall, slick with damp. Chips of limestone litter the treads.
The bailey is an open court of broken stone and patches of grass. A low well curb sits dry near the center.
A wide street runs beneath faded facades with ornate iron balconies. Many of the balconies have collapsed, leaving jagged anchors.
Shallow arcades line the street, their arches chipped and stained. Bits of colored tile still cling to the lower walls.
Tall shutters hang open or lie broken along the street. A few carved lintels remain, softened by weather.
The avenue is paved in broad stones worn smooth by time. A row of bent iron lamps leans over the gutter.
The street widens near a cluster of fallen columns and brick. Dried vines lace across the cracked masonry.
A low room opens onto the street, its counter broken and bare. Stained glass fragments glimmer in the dust.
Small tables have rotted away, leaving only rusted hooks in the floor. A decorative mirror hangs cracked above a cold hearth.
A heavy collapse has split this chamber, exposing the sky. Slabs of stone lie piled in the center.
A narrow passage runs through broken walls, half open to the air. Rubble mounds force the path to one side.
This open yard is choked with split stone and mortar dust. A collapsed crane frame lies among the weeds.
The drawbridge sags at its chains, its planks split and dark. A dry moat lies beneath, scattered with fallen stone.
Half-raised walls stand in a rectangle, their courses uneven and cracked. Old scaffolding poles lie snapped across the ground.
A narrow entryway is blocked by a fallen lintel and drifted rubble. Faded plaster still shows hints of old paint.
A narrow passage squeezes between two thick walls of stone. The floor is polished smooth where many feet once passed.
A low shack of stone holds a cold forge and a broken anvil. Rust flakes glitter across the hearth.
An unfinished structure lies open to the weather, its walls buckled. Bundles of warped timber rot along the edges.
A shallow pit is filled with shattered blocks and silt. A toppled winch frame rests against the wall.
Loose courses of stone mark the outline of a forgotten build. Wind has piled grit against a fallen beam.
A wide chamber opens in the keep, its floor swept bare by wind. A carved niche stands empty above a cracked ledge.
A once-grand hall stands here, its pillars chipped and dim. Faded motifs curl along the walls like ghosts of paint.
Low stalls line the walls, their timber slats collapsed and gray. A trough sits dry beneath a broken window.
The lane opens toward the outer wall, its paving split and worn. A heap of fallen bricks blocks one old doorway.
Two heavy doors hang ajar, their iron hinges rusted thick. A draft moves through the cracked threshold.
A quiet room holds a few toppled chairs and a cracked mosaic floor. The walls are stained with old smoke and damp.
A small altar of stone stands against the wall, its carvings softened. Dried petals lie scattered in the dust.
Broken statues lean against the south wall, their faces worn blank. Fragments of marble litter the floor.
The remains of carved figures crowd the north wall in silent rows. Lichen spreads across their fractured bases.
